pf.rules.written contract: The business's own contract, filled in from the quote, signed by the customer and the business before money is taken, for every quoted event (parties, weddings, company parties). pf.rules.date hold: A quoted event's date stays saved while the contract is signed: up to 24 hours (weddings: 48 hours, the owner's setting).
pf.rules.venue rules: Each venue's rules on file: load-in time and door, parking, power, sound limit, music curfew and load-out time, insurance needed. A venue not on file: the owner checks them before booking.
pf.rules.noise and curfew: Music never runs past the venue's curfew or the local noise rules, even for paid overtime. Outdoors, the venue's earlier outdoor limit applies.
pf.rules.permits and age rules: A permit for an outdoor or public event, an age limit at a bar, or a background check for a school: switches from the venue or the state form.
pf.rules.one a day: One wedding a day per lead DJ, booked up to 18 months ahead (the owner's settings).
pf.rules.cancel schedule: Free to cancel until 24 hours before (the owner's setting). After that, a dated schedule from the contract, never more than the deposit unless the contract says so. One free date change with 14 days' notice, if a DJ is free.
pf.rules.clips and photos: Clips or photos of the event are posted only with the customer's signed yes. A child's only with a parent's yes. No answer means no.
pf.rules.rentals: A signed rental agreement before a first rental, a card saved for damage at pick-up, and late returns as the agreement says.
pf.rules.records: Contracts, venue rules, rental agreements and payments kept 7 years, as for every kind of work.
pf.rules.weather: An outdoor event has a rain plan. The owner sets a weather limit (the example: heavy rain or storms in the forecast); over it, the owner is asked the afternoon before to keep it under the rain plan or move it.

pf.edges.all: Every edge case is handled the general way. These matter most for DJs:
DJ work: Asked to play longer: overtime only with a written yes, and never past the venue's curfew
The lead DJ can't come: a trusted stand-in, or a full refund if the customer wants it
A venue not on file: the owner checks its rules before booking
The venue needs an insurance certificate naming it: a to-do for the owner before the venue's date
Rain on an outdoor event: the rain plan, called the afternoon before
The music form isn't in on time: the DJ covers it on the planning call
The rest isn't paid on its day: one pay link, then the owner decides
A crowd gets unsafe: the DJ stops the music and tells the venue's staff
Guest requests: the do-not-play list always wins
A rented speaker comes back late or damaged: the agreement, and the owner's OK for any charge
